<action type="say">
My system still can’t find any American Airlines flight AA9999 on 2025-12-20, even with the route Madrid → New York and a morning departure. When this happens, it’s usually because:

- The flight number is different in the official schedule on that date (it may have been renumbered or is seasonal).
- It’s a codeshare (for example operated by Iberia or British Airways) and this system only sees the operating carrier’s flight number.
- The filed route uses specific airports that differ from what we’re assuming (e.g., MAD → JFK vs. MAD → EWR).

Here’s how you can quickly verify it:

1) On American Airlines’ website/app  
   - Go to “Flight status”.  
   - From: MAD (Madrid-Barajas).  
   - To: Try JFK first; if nothing appears, also try EWR.  
   - Date: 20 December 2025.  
   - Time: Filter to morning flights.  
   This will show all AA and AA‑codeshare flights for that morning and their correct flight numbers.

2) In your booking confirmation  
   - Open the email or PDF itinerary you received when you booked.  
   - Look for:  
     - Exact airports (e.g., “Madrid (MAD)” and “New York (JFK)” or “Newark (EWR)”), and  
     - The flight number as printed there (it might show something like IBxxxx or BAxxxx, or a different AA number).

If you can paste here exactly what you see in the confirmation for that segment (airline, flight number, and airports), or share your record locator/confirmation code (e.g., ABC123, with personal details removed), I can then:

- Identify the exact flight in the official schedule, and  
- Once we’re close to the travel date, help you check real‑time status (delays, gate, terminal, etc.) and interpret what it means for your plans.</action>
